blocks.prompt: 6 Find the dimensions of the rectangle with greatest perimeter that can be inscribed in the ellipse \(\frac{x^2}{16} + \frac{y^2}{9} = 1\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh maximum (sab se bari qeemat) wala sawal hai: ellipse ke andar aisa rectangle banana hai jis ke kone ellipse par hon aur jis ka perimeter sab se zyada ho.
Kone ko ek hi variable se likhne ke liye parametric point \((4\cos\theta, 3\sin\theta)\) sab se aasaan hai, kyunke yeh har \(\theta\) par khud ba khud ellipse par hota hai.
Plan: perimeter ko \(\theta\) ka function banayein, derivative zero karein, aur second derivative se tasdeeq karein ke yeh maximum hai.
Dhyan rahe ke sawal perimeter ka hai, area ka nahi; dono ke jawab mukhtalif hain.
Rectangle ellipse ke andar 'inscribed' hai, yani us ke charon kone ellipse par hain aur sides axes ke parallel.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\frac{x^2}{16} + \frac{y^2}{9} = 1\) (\(a = 4\), \(b = 3\)).
Maloom karna: andar bane rectangle ki lambai aur chaurai jab perimeter sab se zyada ho.
Tareeqa: ellipse dono axes ke gird symmetric hai, is liye rectangle ka centre origin aur sides axes ke parallel. Pehle quadrant wala kona \((4\cos\theta, 3\sin\theta)\), \(0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\).

Sides aur perimeter
Baaqi kone \((-4\cos\theta, 3\sin\theta)\), \((-4\cos\theta, -3\sin\theta)\), \((4\cos\theta, -3\sin\theta)\) hain. To lambai \(= 8\cos\theta\), chaurai \(= 6\sin\theta\).
\[P(\theta) = 2(8\cos\theta + 6\sin\theta)\]
\[= 16\cos\theta + 12\sin\theta\]
Kyun: perimeter = 2(lambai + chaurai). Kone se doosre kone tak x mein \(4\cos\theta - (-4\cos\theta) = 8\cos\theta\).

Derivative zero karein
\[P'(\theta) = -16\sin\theta + 12\cos\theta = 0\]
\[\tan\theta = \frac{12}{16} = \frac{3}{4}\]
Kyun: maximum par curve ki dhalaan (slope) zero hoti hai. \(\cos\) ka derivative \(-\sin\), aur \(\sin\) ka \(\cos\).

\(\sin\theta\), \(\cos\theta\) nikalein
\[\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}, \quad \cos\theta = \frac{4}{5}\]
Kyun: \(\theta\) acute hai; 3, 4, 5 wale right triangle mein \(\tan\theta = \frac{3}{4}\), to \(\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}\), \(\cos\theta = \frac{4}{5}\).

Second derivative test
\[P''(\theta) = -16\cos\theta - 12\sin\theta\]
\[= -\frac{64}{5} - \frac{36}{5} = -20 < 0\]
Kyun: second derivative negative ho to woh point maximum hota hai (curve neeche ki taraf mur rahi hai).

Dimensions
\[\text{length} = 8 \cdot \frac{4}{5} = \frac{32}{5}\]
\[\text{width} = 6 \cdot \frac{3}{5} = \frac{18}{5}\]
\[P = 2\left(\frac{32}{5} + \frac{18}{5}\right) = 20\]
Kyun: cos aur sin ki qeematein rakh di.
Dhyan dein: jawab kone ke coordinates \(\frac{16}{5}\), \(\frac{9}{5}\) nahi; sides un ki dugni hain.

Ek nazar mein
Maximum ya minimum wale ellipse ke sawalon mein parametric point \((a\cos\theta, b\sin\theta)\) sab se kaam ka auzaar (tool) hai, kyunke do variables \(x, y\) ki jagah ek hi variable \(\theta\) reh jata hai. Phir aam calculus: derivative zero, aur second derivative se maximum ki tasdeeq.

Tasdeeq
Kona \(\left(\frac{16}{5}, \frac{9}{5}\right)\) ellipse par hai: \(\frac{16}{25} + \frac{9}{25} = 1\). Bina calculus ke: \(16\cos\theta + 12\sin\theta = 20\cos(\theta - \alpha)\), jahan \(\cos\alpha = \frac{4}{5}\); is ki sab se bari qeemat 20 hai.
Kyun: do raaston se ek hi maximum 20 aaya.
